content: Homepage Latest News Cuba News Miami News Blackouts today Informal Exchange Rate Videos Sports International News Opinion CiberCuba Interviews United States Cuisine Florida Spain Culture Motor Readings Tourism History Nature Health Close the sidebar ESENFRIT Guantánamo acknowledges an increase in Aedes aegypti and points out shortcomings in the detection of febrile cases Latest News By CiberCuba Editorial Team Friday, August 14, 2026 - 5:54 PM The municipalities of Guantánamo, Caimanera, San Antonio del Sur, El Salvador, and Niceto Pérez have the highest concentration of mosquitoesPhoto © Venceremos The political and health authorities of Guantánamo acknowledged this Friday a worsening of the epidemiological situation in the province, characterized by an increase in the presence of the Aedes aegypti mosquito and shortcomings in the detection of febrile cases. The First Secretary of the Communist Party in the region, Yoel Pérez García, called for a meeting with health officials, which was also attended by Governor Alis Azahares Torreblanca, and demanded greater efforts in the fight against vector-borne diseases, reported the official newspaper Venceremos. Pérez identified the lack of researchers as a critical factor. According to the official, completing this workforce is "decisive" for increasing the detection of fever cases and achieving better control of the mosquito transmission hotspots, although the media refrained from releasing statistics on the matter. The governor, for her part, emphasized "the importance of the functioning of leadership positions and multidisciplinary work to win the battle against such a dangerous vector, responsible for diseases that can become fatal, such as dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, and Zika." The municipalities of Guantánamo, Caimanera, San Antonio del Sur, El Salvador, and Niceto Pérez have been identified as the most affected by the presence of Aedes aegypti. Authorities consider it more urgent to conduct health hearings and educational talks in these areas to guide the population on the elimination of breeding sites and to seek medical consultation in the presence of fever symptoms. The same meeting critically analyzed the performance of the Maternal and Child Program so far this year, with a notably negative impact in the municipalities of Guantánamo, Baracoa, Manuel Tames, and El Salvador. The alert comes after weeks of sustained deterioration. At the end of July, Guantánamo reported 23 suspected cases of dengue, and the municipalities of Imías and San Antonio del Sur were classified at the Epidemiological Alarm level, the highest risk tier within the Cuban endemic channel before declaring an epidemic. On August 10, Radio Guantánamo was already reporting an upward trend in febrile cases in the capital city, with 18 suspected cases of dengue primarily concentrated in the southern area, in addition to confirmed circulation of serotypes 2, 3, and 4 of the virus. The provincial scenario is set against the backdrop of a national health crisis. In June, the Deputy Minister of Public Health, Carilda Peña, publicly warned that Cuba could face a new dengue epidemic due to the simultaneous circulation of all four serotypes of the virus. Structural factors exacerbate the problem, such as prolonged blackouts that force families to store water in containers, which become breeding grounds for mosquitoes. The collapse of the waste collection system due to a lack of fuel promotes their proliferation, and the shortage of insecticides halts fumigation efforts in much of the country. Guantánamo has a recurring history as one of the provinces most affected by dengue. In October 2022, it was identified as the first territory in the country for dengue transmission, with nearly 1,600 deposits containing Aedes aegypti larvae in more than 1,300 homes across nine municipalities. According to data from the Pan American Health Organization, Cuba ended 2025 with over 81,900 cases of dengue and chikungunya and at least 65 fatalities associated with both diseases, figures that the Ministry of Public Health took months to publicly acknowledge. content: English Kerala Travel Guides & Travelogues Communicable Diseases Rise in Keralam as 11,921 Seek Treatment for Fever in a Single Day Image used for representation Web Desk Published on Aug 13, 2026, 11:47 AM | 2 min read Thiruvananthapuram : Communicable diseases are on the rise in Keralam, with a large number of people seeking treatment for fever, chikungunya, dengue fever and leptospirosis over the past week. According to Health Department figures, 11,921 people sought treatment for fever across the state on Tuesday alone. As many as 156 people were admitted to hospitals for observation. Malappuram recorded the highest number of fever cases, with 2,961 outpatient cases reported. Infectious Diseases On Tuesday alone, 92 people tested positive for dengue fever in the state. Palakkad recorded the highest number with 19 cases, followed by Thiruvananthapuram with 18, Thrissur with 15 and Ernakulam with 11. A total of 264 suspected dengue cases were also reported. Leptospirosis was confirmed in 17 people across the state, while two deaths due to the disease were reported on Tuesday. The deaths occurred in Thrissur and Malappuram districts. Jaundice was confirmed in 33 people on Tuesday. The state also recorded 1,979 cases of diarrhoeal diseases and 145 cases of influenza. Chickenpox was reported in 83 people, while three cases of shigella and eight cases of malaria were also recorded. A total of 1,09,087 people have sought treatment for fever in the state this month. Two fever-related deaths have also been reported. So far this month, dengue fever has been confirmed in 902 people. Leptospirosis has been confirmed in 147 people, with 10 deaths reported. Keralam has recorded 271 cases of jaundice in August. As many as 17,198 diarrhoeal disease cases and 983 influenza cases have been confirmed, while 16 influenza-related deaths have been reported. Chickenpox has been confirmed in 812 people this month alone. With rain and rain-related disasters continuing, people have been advised to remain vigilant against communicable diseases. Boiled and cooled water should be used. Those who have come into contact with stagnant water should take doxycycline as a preventive medicine against leptospirosis. People with cough or sneezing should wear masks. Those suffering from fever should not resort to self-medication. ORS should be taken as advised if symptoms of diarrhoea occur. Food should be consumed while it is hot. People with lifestyle diseases should ensure that they take their medicines regularly. Pets should be kept away from relief camps as far as possible. Well water should be chlorinated using bleaching powder. Special care should be given to children, pregnant women and palliative care patients. T’puram: Preventive and control measures against vector-borne diseases have been intensified in various wards under the Vattiyoorkavu family health centre (FHC) following the reporting of an increase in chikungunya and dengue cases, said the district medical officer.As many as 54 chikungunya cases and 87 dengue cases were reported in Vattiyoorkavu area during June and July. A detailed action plan has been prepared to contain the spread of diseases, with source reduction, fogging, and awareness campaigns being carried out at the field level.A special review meeting led by the DMO will be held at the Vattiyoorkavu FHC on Friday to assess and plan further preventive measures.In Vazhotukonam ward, which reported a higher number of chikungunya cases, the vector control unit, Vattiyoorkavu FHC public health staff and Asha workers carried out continuous preventive activities for a week. These efforts have resulted in a significant decline in chikungunya cases in the area, officials said.In Kodunganoor ward, where dengue cases were reported, a rapid response team meeting was held under the chairmanship of the health standing committee chairperson. A mass source-reduction drive was subsequently conducted under the leadership of the mayor. Health workers, Asha and anganwadi workers, corporation employees, haritha Karma Sena members and representatives of residents’ associations participated in the drive. by Taboolaby Taboola Sponsored LinksSponsored Links Promoted LinksPromoted Links You May Like Cardiologist Warns: "Avoid Bottled Water at All Costs"Healthy LifeStyle 101 Undo In Nettayam ward, an RRT meeting was held under the chairmanship of the ward councillor to coordinate dengue-control measures. Intensive source-reduction activities, distribution of awareness leaflets, and fogging were carried out with the participation of voluntary organisations and local community groups.The DMO said that dengue and chikungunya are currently under control in the area. The public was urged to fully cooperate with the preventive measures being carried out jointly by the health department and local self-govt institutions.Health advisoryChikungunya and dengue are transmitted by aedes mosquitoes, which breed in stagnant, clean water. Residents should inspect their homes, surroundings and institutions at least once a week, and eliminate potential mosquito-breeding sites.The DMO urged people to observe ‘dry day’ on Fridays in schools, Saturdays at workplaces and Sundays at homes.Those experiencing symptoms such as high fever, severe joint pain, headache or chills should avoid self-medication and seek treatment at the nearest health centre immediately, the DMO advised.
